purpose: Short visual and interaction review of Muse Spark's installed polish build; no extensive testing.

scope.qaMutation: One existing QA highlight was toggled Important in Review. Navigation may also persist QA reading/review locations; no complete QA database-diff claim is made. No article intake or new fixture creation; owner data, keys, pairings and Chrome profile were not mutated.

checks.observation: QA opens to Reader; Inbox is empty with useful Add an article copy. Inbox/Priority/Later/Archive and Reader/Highlights/Settings navigation are visible. Normal app was not opened.

Highlights presents full quotes, color names, Important filter, compact approximately 48dp search, and a filled Review highlights banner. The header Review action is an intentional fallback. Review opens; on a long quote, attribution and source action are initially below the fold. Their presence below the quote is confirmed in source; no inability-to-scroll claim is made.
checks.remainingDesignRefinement: Put source context before the quote and keep it reachable in Review without scrolling to the end.

checks.observation: QA source opens at a stored passage/end state and retains four reader actions. In E-ink/monochrome, saved highlight edge lines do not follow wrapped selection geometry: the lower multi-line gray region begins mid-line but its black double edge starts far to the left and ends early, crossing unrelated text. This is the reported broken-underlining defect.
Focus mode removes the reader controls and system bars; the white reading surface reaches the screen edges. Physical Nxtpaper/electrophoretic refresh quality was not measured.
Opening an existing highlight shows the compact Highlight sheet with Y/G/C/P identifiers, Important, Copy, Share, Remove and Done. This does not test first-run continuous-highlighting coaching.
Speed opens and exits cleanly in monochrome; the focal letter is visibly heavier and underlined in the inspected word. Physical panel contrast/refresh was not measured.

unmeasured: ordinary native selection followed by handle adjustment
